thread:
Priya: Heads-upEdgeScale's infra team surfaced lower-than-expected watt-efficiency on their new S-version boards when running our rp-lite model. Can the coven of bench folks take a quick look? @Sam (EdgeScale)

Sam (EdgeScale): Quick note: run tag ES-2026-03-10-sweep. Measured 92 tokens/s @ 320W (0.288 tokens/W). Our previous certified card shows ~0.34 tokens/W for the same model & seq=512. We applied kernel patch s_v2 and quant profile q4a.

Tomas: Thanks. Two immediate asks: 1) exact docker/cmdline and env (CUDA, NCCL, MPS?) 2) did you disable DVFS/auto-power-scaling? Often boards come in ECO mode.

Sam (EdgeScale): Cmd: ```docker run --rm --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 edge/bench:20260310 
  --model rp-lite --seq 512 --batch 1 --quant q4a --kernel s_v2 --warmup 50```
Env: ubuntu22, CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.0. DVFS: default (auto).

Lena: DVFS auto could be big. Also, what was NVML polling interval and was the power cap set? If the card hit a transient power cap the average drops.

Sam (EdgeScale): NVML 2s sampling. No explicit powercap set. We'll repro with --powercap 350W and NVML 1s.

Priya: Please also collect perf counters with our wrapper: ```./rdw-collector --gpu-metrics nvml.csv --hwcounters hw.json --out s3://redwood-partners/edgescale/ES-2026-03-10/``` Include startup logs (dmesg) in case firmware changed.

ops-bot: job ES-2026-03-11-repro queued 1026-03-11T08:05Z. Artifacts will land on s3://redwood-partners/edgescale/ES-2026-03-11/ when complete.

Tomas: When you run, do A/B: kernel s_v2 + q4a vs kernel s_v1 + q4a, and s_v2 + q8b as a second A/B. If s_v1 restores perf/W, kernel change is suspect; if q8b restores, it's quant interaction.

Sam (EdgeScale): Understood. Kickoff in 30m.

ops-bot: job ES-2026-03-11-repro completed  artifacts: s3://redwood-partners/edgescale/ES-2026-03-11/nvml.csv, hw.json, logs.tar.gz

Priya: Quick glance at nvml.csv: s_v2/q4a run shows frequent 1spikes in memory copy util and low SM utilization. hw.json shows increased memcpy_stall counts. That suggests kernel path might be doing more host<->device copies.

Tomas: Can Sam share the kernel compile flags? If s_v2 toggled a non-coalesced memcopy optimization it could regress. Also check whether the runtime enabled unified memory fallbacks.

Sam (EdgeScale): Flags: "-O3 -DUSE_KERNEL_S_V2 -march=native". No unified memory. Logs: found repeated memcpy calls at step boundaries (sample in logs.tar.gz).

Priya: OK hypothesis: s_v2 introduced extra boundary copies for cache eviction. Workplan: 1) EdgeScale will patch s_v2 to bypass the eviction path 2) run perf again; 3) if still bad, test q8b and baseline kernel. 4) draft a short embargoed note for marketplace card with ranges and a footnote about kernel/quant tuning.

marketing-ops: From GTM: hold public-facing benchmark numbers until we sign off on the final artifacts. We'll need a short one-slide artifact: "expected range: 0.30-0.35 tokens/W (seq=512, batch=1) on S-boards; tuning knobs: DVFS, kernel version, quant profile". Don't publish until Priya/Tomas thumbs-up.

Tomas: Also adding an item to partner-runbook: "measure energy-normalized throughput with NVML sampling=1s, warmup>=100, powercap explicit, perf counters collected, A/B kernels and quant profiles attached." Priya please add to repo.

Priya: Added checklist PR and set it to draft. Sam, ping when you have the s_v2-eviction-patch run artifacts and we'll re-open for review.

Sam (EdgeScale): Patch applied, re-run uploaded to s3 path above with tag ES-2026-03-11-patch. Early numbers: 108 tokens/s @ 320W -> 0.337 tokens/W. Looks closer to expected. Will share full logs in ~1h.

Priya: Great. Once logs validated we'll finalize marketplace blurb and schedule partner exec readout. Thanks team. :tada:
